report.title: Red Lions edge Blue Sharks 3-2 after extra-time swings
report.summary: Red Lions beat Blue Sharks 3-2 after extra time in a match that went 1-0 to Red Lions through Fox in the 28th minute, 1-1 through Gray in the 62nd, 2-1 through Reid in the 95th, and 2-2 through Cruz in the 105th before Bell’s own goal in the 113th minute put Red Lions back in front. The game was played at a high tempo with repeated lead changes, and Red Lions finished with the stronger numbers in possession, territory, chances, and passing.

sections.text: Red Lions kept finding a way back into control every time Blue Sharks clawed their way level. Fox started it, Gray and Cruz kept the tension alive, Reid gave Red Lions hope again in extra time, and then Bell’s own goal in the 113th minute sent the game into its final Red Lions lead. It was frantic, nerve-racking, and never settled until the end.

Red Lions controlled the match overall with 69% possession, 85% field tilt, 776 completed passes at 93% accuracy, and 27 shots to Blue Sharks’ 15. Red Lions also led expected goals 4.61 to 2.48, with 11 shots on target and 6 big chances compared with Blue Sharks’ 7 shots on target and 5 big chances. In the last 10 minutes Red Lions had 79% possession and 91% of final-third actions, while Blue Sharks were limited to 21% possession and 9% field tilt.

Red Lions won 3-2 after extra time in a match that swung back and forth throughout. Fox put Red Lions ahead in the 28th minute from Lane’s assist, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks in the 62nd, Reid restored Red Lions’ lead in the 95th from Rook’s pass, and Cruz made it 2-2 in the 105th with Wells assisting. Bell’s own goal in the 113th minute left Red Lions ahead at the final whistle.

fan.title: Red Lions survive a wild extra-time battle to beat Blue Sharks 3-2
paragraphs: Red Lions took the lead through Fox in the 28th minute, but Blue Sharks kept hanging in and Gray levelled in the 62nd minute. Red Lions went back ahead when Reid scored in the 95th minute, only for Cruz to bring Blue Sharks level in the 105th minute.

The match turned on territory and pressure. Red Lions had 69% of the possession over the full game, completed 776 passes at 93% accuracy, and spent long spells on the front foot, while Blue Sharks were forced deeper and could not sustain control for long. In the last 10 minutes Red Lions were overwhelming, with 79% of the ball and 91% of the action in the final third, but the closing spell was still messy and open.

The decisive moment came in the 113th minute when Bell put into his own net, giving Red Lions the goal that finally settled a chaotic contest. Red Lions finished with more shots, more big chances, and the sharper edge in extra time, while Blue Sharks kept fighting right to the end.

paragraphs: Red Lions won 3-2 after extra time in a match that flipped back and forth all night. Fox put Red Lions ahead in the 28th minute from Lane’s assist, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks in the 62nd from Frost’s pass, and Reid restored the lead in the 95th minute before Cruz replied in the 105th with Wells assisting.

Red Lions controlled the match overall. Red Lions had 69% possession, 85% of final-third action, and completed 776 of 838 passes at 93% accuracy, while Blue Sharks were limited to 31% possession and 15% of the territory. Over the full match, Red Lions created more volume with 27 shots, 11 on target and 6 big chances, compared with Blue Sharks’ 15 shots, 7 on target and 5 big chances.

The turning point came in the closing stretch, when Red Lions kept forcing play high up the pitch and Gray’s own goal in the 113th minute put Red Lions back in front for good. The late spell was chaotic, but Red Lions’ pressure over the whole match and especially in extra time finally tilted a wild contest their way.

broadcaster.title: Red Lions edge a frantic extra-time battle
paragraphs: Red Lions won 3-2 after extra time in a match that swung back and forth throughout. Fox put Red Lions ahead in the 28th minute from Lane’s assist, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks in the 62nd, and Reid restored Red Lions’ lead in the 95th from Rook’s pass.

Blue Sharks forced it back to 2-2 through Cruz in the 105th minute, assisted by Wells, before Bell put the ball into Red Lions’ net for an own goal in the 113th minute, with Red Lions credited with the goal. That proved the turning point in a finish full of tension and mistakes.

Red Lions controlled most of the contest, with 69% of the possession, 85% of the territory and 110 final-third entries, while Blue Sharks stayed in touch through a more direct, less frequent threat. The closing spell was chaotic, but Red Lions kept spending more time in Blue Sharks’ half and finally came through in a game they won on the balance of pressure and chances.
